scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Javier Gonzalez and I'm 65. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Mr. Gonzalez. I'm sorry to hear about the confusion regarding your billing while you were away. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and the email is j.gonzalez@email.com.
Thank you, Mr. Gonzalez. I have located your account. For security purposes, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file?

Thank you for verifying those details. I see the cancellation was processed on the 34th day. While our 'Service Agreement Policy 4.2' strictly limits automated refunds to 30 days, I can see your account has been in good standing for three years. Given your circumstances, I have received authorization to make a one-time exception for you.
Oh, that is a huge relief. Thank you so much for understanding.

You are very welcome, Mr. Gonzalez. I have successfully processed the refund for the charge of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit appear in your account within 3-5 business days. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account details and applied a one-time policy exception based on the customer's long-standing account history, successfully issuing the refund.
